subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: Should gateway startup keep failing fast on required SecretRef failures, add bounded generic in-process retry/backoff, or introduce configurable degraded/circuit-breaker behavior for exec secret providers?
rationale: The source path is clear, but changing startup SecretRef behavior affects fail-closed security posture, external credential-provider side effects, service restart behavior, and possibly new config/default surface.

options.title: Bounded Generic Retry
options.body: Add a small default startup retry/backoff around SecretRef snapshot preparation, keep final failure fail-closed, and document supervisor restart-storm guidance.

options.title: Document And Keep Fail-Fast
options.body: Preserve current fail-fast semantics and rely on supervisor limits, external resolvers such as Varlock, and docs to avoid provider-rate amplification.

options.title: Configurable Degraded Mode
options.body: Add explicit operator-controlled circuit/degraded behavior for exec providers, accepting a larger config and security review surface.

recommendation.title: Bounded Generic Retry
recommendation.body: Add a small default startup retry/backoff around SecretRef snapshot preparation, keep final failure fail-closed, and document supervisor restart-storm guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is closest to the SecretRef provider and eager runtime snapshot history that this person introduced and expanded.
